title: Polyclinic video consultations for acute conditions and expansion plans
asked: Mr David Hoe asked whether all polyclinics currently offer video consultations for non-emergency acute conditions, whether those that do not will introduce them, and the expected timelines for implementation.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said polyclinic video consultations are generally limited to patients who had previously attended in person and for specific indications such as follow-up of minor acute conditions, reviewing test results or monitoring recovery. If new or worsening conditions are identified, the video consultation will not proceed and the patient will be advised to seek an in-person consultation. Teleconsultations for common acute symptoms like cough and cold with medical certificate issuance are not typically offered, and while SingHealth Polyclinics offers the service under a cluster-run pilot, there are no immediate plans for broad-based expansion across all polyclinics. In supplementary replies, he said all three clusters offer video consultation for follow-up acute conditions, SingHealth's first-attendance acute service remains a pilot with no current expansion plans, the other two clusters are focusing on chronic disease management including telehealth, and the pilot's 18-year-old age cut-off is a cautious approach; MOH issues broad telehealth guidelines and providers assess suitability holistically.

key_points.quote: SingHealth is taking this 18-years-old cut-off as a more cautious approach to ensure that only adults are included in the testing of this service

key_points.point: MOH issues circulars to service providers on how to use and structure telehealth services, and gives broad guidance rather than prescriptive line-by-line rules.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: there are circulars issued by the Ministry to the service providers regarding how they should use telehealth services and how they should structure those services

key_points.point: Providers assess patients' suitability for telehealth holistically, including condition, age and ability to communicate, and are given latitude to exercise judgement.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: providers assess patients' suitability for telehealth holistically, including their condition, their age, their ability to communicate using telehealth
